+         print(f"Backup:  {self.backup_root.absolute()}")

+         # Create backup structure

+         
+         # Remove violations
+         self.remove_violations()
+         
+         # Remove cache files
+         self.remove_cache_files()
+         
+         # Generate and save report
+         report = self.generate_report()
+         report_file = "violation_removal_report.txt"
+         with open(report_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

+         
+         print(report)

+         
+         return report

+ Script to Replace Anatomical Constraint Violations with Correct Samples
+ 
+ This script:
+ 1. Backs up 23 violating files from regurgitationV1 to violations_backup
+ 2. Replaces them with correct (non-violating) files from the same dataset
+ 3. Maintains the same filename structure
+ 4. Generates a detailed replacement report
+ 
+ Strategy:
+ - For each violating file, find a non-violating replacement from the same split
+ - Keep the original violating filename
+ - Backup original files before replacement
+ """
+ 
+ import os
+ import shutil
+ import random
+ from pathlib import Path
+ from datetime import datetime
+ from collections import defaultdict
+ 
+ 
+ class ViolationReplacer:
+     def __init__(self, dataset_root="regurgitationV1", backup_root="violations_backup"):
+         self.dataset_root = Path(dataset_root)
+         self.backup_root = Path(backup_root)
+         self.replacements = {"train": [], "valid": [], "test": []}
+         self.errors = []
+         
+         # Violation list with their constraint types
+         self.violations = {
+             "train": {
+                 "ZmNmwq5saG5m-unnamed_1_3.mp4-8": "PSAX_MR",
+                 "ZmVrwqtpbMKawpw=-unnamed_1_2.mp4-26": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmVrwqtpbMKawpw=-unnamed_2_1.mp4-15": "PSAX_MR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-0": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-1": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-10": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-17": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-9": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "bWplwqlsaMKZ-unnamed_1_1.mp4-1": "A4C_AR",
+                 "bWplwqlsaMKZ-unnamed_1_1.mp4-2": "A4C_AR",
+                 "bWplwqlsaMKZ-unnamed_1_1.mp4-28": "PSAX_AR",
+                 "bWplwqlsaMKZ-unnamed_1_1.mp4-3": "A4C_AR",
+                 "bWplwqlsaMKZ-unnamed_1_1.mp4-39": "PSAX_AR",
+             },
+             "valid": {
+                 "ZmRnwqZla8Kcwp4=-unnamed_2_2.mp4-35": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-12": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "a2lrwqduZsKc-unnamed_1_1.mp4-31": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "ZmZnwqlqbMKawp0=-unnamed_1_1.mp4-4": "A4C_PR",
+             },
+             "test": {
+                 "ZmNlwq5mZcKcwps=-unnamed_1_1.mp4-0": "PSAX_AR",
+                 "ZmZnwqlqbMKawp0=-unnamed_1_1.mp4-15": "A4C_PR",
+                 "ZmZnwqlqbMKawp0=-unnamed_1_1.mp4-17": "A4C_PR",
+                 "ZmZnwqlqbMKawp0=-unnamed_1_1.mp4-21": "A4C_PR",
+                 "ZmhmwqduY8KU-Mmode+2D+Doppler_Echo_color_1_2.mp4-13": "PLAX_TR",
+                 "bWplwqlsaMKZ-unnamed_1_1.mp4-14": "A4C_AR",
+             }
+         }
+         
+         # Class mappings
+         self.view_classes = {"A4C": 0, "PSAX": 1, "PLAX": 2}
+         self.regurg_classes = {"MR": 0, "TR": 1, "AR": 2, "PR": 3}
+         
+         # Anatomical constraints: view -> allowed regurgitations
+         self.allowed_regurg = {
+             "A4C": ["MR", "TR"],    # Apical 4-Chamber
+             "PSAX": ["PR", "TR"],   # Parasternal Short Axis
+             "PLAX": ["AR", "MR"]    # Parasternal Long Axis
+         }
+ 
+     def parse_label_file(self, label_path):
+         """Parse YOLOv5 label file to extract view and detections"""
+         if not label_path.exists():
+             return None, []
+         
+         with open(label_path, 'r') as f:
+             lines = f.readlines()
+         
+         # Last line should be classification: view_class has_regurg regurg_present
+         view_class = None
+         detections = []
+         
+         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+             parts = line.strip().split()
+             if len(parts) == 0:
+                 continue
+             
+             # Detection line: class_id x y w h (5 values) or class_id x1 y1 x2 y2 x3 y3 x4 y4 (9 values for rotated)
+             if len(parts) >= 5:
+                 class_id = int(parts[0])
+                 detections.append(class_id)
+             # Classification line: view_class has_regurg regurg_present
+             elif len(parts) == 3 and i == len(lines) - 1:
+                 view_class = int(parts[0])
+         
+         return view_class, detections
+ 
+     def check_constraint_violation(self, view_class, detections):
+         """Check if a file violates anatomical constraints"""
+         if view_class is None:
+             return False, None
+         
+         view_name = [k for k, v in self.view_classes.items() if v == view_class]
+         if not view_name:
+             return False, None
+         view_name = view_name[0]
+         
+         allowed = [self.regurg_classes[r] for r in self.allowed_regurg[view_name]]
+         
+         for det_class in detections:
+             if det_class not in allowed:
+                 regurg_name = [k for k, v in self.regurg_classes.items() if v == det_class][0]
+                 return True, f"{view_name}_{regurg_name}"
+         
+         return False, None
+ 
+     def find_non_violating_files(self, split):
+         """Find all non-violating files in a split"""
+         labels_dir = self.dataset_root / split / "labels"
+         if not labels_dir.exists():
+             return []
+         
+         non_violating = []
+         violating_basenames = set(self.violations[split].keys())
+         
+         for label_file in labels_dir.glob("*.txt"):
+             basename = label_file.stem
+             
+             # Skip if it's in the violation list
+             if basename in violating_basenames:
+                 continue
+             
+             # Check if it violates constraints
+             view_class, detections = self.parse_label_file(label_file)
+             if view_class is not None:
+                 is_violation, _ = self.check_constraint_violation(view_class, detections)
+                 if not is_violation:
+                     non_violating.append(basename)
+         
+         return non_violating
+ 
+     def create_backup_structure(self):
+         """Create backup directory structure"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("Creating backup directory structure...")
+         print("="*70)
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             (self.backup_root / split / "images").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+             (self.backup_root / split / "labels").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+         
+         print(f"✓ Backup directory created at: {self.backup_root.absolute()}")
+ 
+     def backup_file(self, split, basename):
+         """Backup a single file pair (image + label)"""
+         image_file = self.dataset_root / split / "images" / f"{basename}.png"
+         label_file = self.dataset_root / split / "labels" / f"{basename}.txt"
+         
+         backup_image = self.backup_root / split / "images" / f"{basename}.png"
+         backup_label = self.backup_root / split / "labels" / f"{basename}.txt"
+         
+         success = True
+         
+         if image_file.exists():
+             shutil.copy2(image_file, backup_image)
+         else:
+             self.errors.append(f"Image not found: {image_file}")
+             success = False
+         
+         if label_file.exists():
+             shutil.copy2(label_file, backup_label)
+         else:
+             self.errors.append(f"Label not found: {label_file}")
+             success = False
+         
+         return success
+ 
+     def replace_file(self, split, old_basename, new_basename):
+         """Replace violating file with a correct one"""
+         # Source (correct file)
+         src_image = self.dataset_root / split / "images" / f"{new_basename}.png"
+         src_label = self.dataset_root / split / "labels" / f"{new_basename}.txt"
+         
+         # Destination (keeping the violating filename)
+         dst_image = self.dataset_root / split / "images" / f"{old_basename}.png"
+         dst_label = self.dataset_root / split / "labels" / f"{old_basename}.txt"
+         
+         success = True
+         
+         try:
+             # Copy correct files to replace violating ones
+             if src_image.exists():
+                 shutil.copy2(src_image, dst_image)
+             else:
+                 self.errors.append(f"Source image not found: {src_image}")
+                 success = False
+             
+             if src_label.exists():
+                 shutil.copy2(src_label, dst_label)
+             else:
+                 self.errors.append(f"Source label not found: {src_label}")
+                 success = False
+         except Exception as e:
+             self.errors.append(f"Error replacing {old_basename} with {new_basename}: {e}")
+             success = False
+         
+         return success
+ 
+     def process_replacements(self):
+         """Process all file replacements"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("PROCESSING VIOLATION REPLACEMENTS")
+         print("="*70)
+         
+         total_replaced = 0
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             print(f"\n[{split.upper()}] Processing {len(self.violations[split])} violations...")
+             
+             # Find non-violating files
+             non_violating = self.find_non_violating_files(split)
+             print(f"  Found {len(non_violating)} non-violating files to use as replacements")
+             
+             if len(non_violating) < len(self.violations[split]):
+                 self.errors.append(
+                     f"Not enough non-violating files in {split}: "
+                     f"need {len(self.violations[split])}, found {len(non_violating)}"
+                 )
+                 continue
+             
+             # Randomly select replacements
+             random.seed(42)  # For reproducibility
+             replacements = random.sample(non_violating, len(self.violations[split]))
+             
+             # Process each violation
+             for i, (violating_basename, violation_type) in enumerate(self.violations[split].items()):
+                 replacement_basename = replacements[i]
+                 
+                 print(f"\n  [{i+1}/{len(self.violations[split])}] {violating_basename}")
+                 print(f"    Violation Type: {violation_type}")
+                 print(f"    Replacement: {replacement_basename}")
+                 
+                 # Backup original
+                 if self.backup_file(split, violating_basename):
+                     print(f"    ✓ Backed up original file")
+                 else:
+                     print(f"    ✗ Failed to backup")
+                     continue
+                 
+                 # Replace with correct file
+                 if self.replace_file(split, violating_basename, replacement_basename):
+                     print(f"    ✓ Replaced with correct file")
+                     self.replacements[split].append({
+                         "old": violating_basename,
+                         "new": replacement_basename,
+                         "type": violation_type
+                     })
+                     total_replaced += 1
+                 else:
+                     print(f"    ✗ Failed to replace")
+         
+         print(f"\n{'='*70}")
+         print(f"TOTAL FILES REPLACED: {total_replaced}")
+         print(f"{'='*70}")
+ 
+     def remove_cache_files(self):
+         """Remove dataset cache files to force regeneration"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("REMOVING DATASET CACHE FILES")
+         print("="*70)
+         
+         cache_patterns = ["*.cache", "*.cache.npy"]
+         removed_caches = []
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             labels_dir = self.dataset_root / split / "labels"
+             if labels_dir.exists():
+                 for pattern in cache_patterns:
+                     for cache_file in labels_dir.glob(pattern):
+                         try:
+                             cache_file.unlink()
+                             removed_caches.append(cache_file)
+                             print(f"  ✓ Removed cache: {cache_file}")
+                         except Exception as e:
+                             self.errors.append(f"Error removing cache {cache_file}: {e}")
+         
+         print(f"\nTotal cache files removed: {len(removed_caches)}")
+ 
+     def generate_report(self):
+         """Generate detailed replacement report"""
+         timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
+         
+         report = f"""
+ {'='*70}
+ ANATOMICAL VIOLATION REPLACEMENT REPORT
+ {'='*70}
+ 
+ Generated: {timestamp}
+ Dataset: {self.dataset_root.absolute()}
+ Backup Location: {self.backup_root.absolute()}
+ 
+ {'='*70}
+ REPLACEMENT SUMMARY
+ {'='*70}
+ 
+ Total Violations: 23
+ Successfully Replaced: {sum(len(r) for r in self.replacements.values())}
+ 
+ By Split:
+ - Train:  {len(self.replacements['train'])} files replaced
+ - Valid:  {len(self.replacements['valid'])} files replaced
+ - Test:   {len(self.replacements['test'])} files replaced
+ 
+ {'='*70}
+ DETAILED REPLACEMENT LIST
+ {'='*70}
+ 
+ """
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             if self.replacements[split]:
+                 report += f"\n{split.upper()}:\n"
+                 report += "-" * 70 + "\n"
+                 for r in self.replacements[split]:
+                     report += f"\nViolation: {r['old']}\n"
+                     report += f"  Type: {r['type']}\n"
+                     report += f"  Replaced with: {r['new']}\n"
+         
+         if self.errors:
+             report += f"\n{'='*70}\n"
+             report += f"ERRORS ENCOUNTERED ({len(self.errors)})\n"
+             report += f"{'='*70}\n\n"
+             for error in self.errors:
+                 report += f"- {error}\n"
+         
+         report += f"\n{'='*70}\n"
+         report += "VIOLATION TYPES REPLACED\n"
+         report += f"{'='*70}\n\n"
+         report += "PLAX_TR: TR detected in PLAX view (NOT ALLOWED) - 10 files\n"
+         report += "A4C_AR:  AR detected in A4C view (NOT ALLOWED) - 4 files\n"
+         report += "A4C_PR:  PR detected in A4C view (NOT ALLOWED) - 4 files\n"
+         report += "PSAX_AR: AR detected in PSAX view (NOT ALLOWED) - 3 files\n"
+         report += "PSAX_MR: MR detected in PSAX view (NOT ALLOWED) - 2 files\n"
+         
+         report += f"\n{'='*70}\n"
+         report += "NEXT STEPS\n"
+         report += f"{'='*70}\n\n"
+         report += "1. Review the backup files in violations_backup/ if needed\n"
+         report += "2. Dataset caches have been cleared\n"
+         report += "3. Dataset now contains only anatomically correct samples\n"
+         report += "4. Ready to retrain with clean dataset\n"
+         report += "5. Use: python train.py --data regurgitationV1/data.yaml\n"
+         report += "\n"
+         
+         return report
+ 
+     def run(self, dry_run=False):
+         """Execute the violation replacement process"""
+         if dry_run:
+             print("\n" + "="*70)
+             print("DRY RUN MODE - No files will be modified")
+             print("="*70)
+             
+             for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+                 print(f"\n{split.upper()}: {len(self.violations[split])} violations")
+                 non_violating = self.find_non_violating_files(split)
+                 print(f"  Available non-violating files: {len(non_violating)}")
+             
+             return
+         
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("STARTING ANATOMICAL VIOLATION REPLACEMENT PROCESS")
+         print("="*70)
+         print(f"Dataset: {self.dataset_root.absolute()}")
+         print(f"Backup:  {self.backup_root.absolute()}")
+         
+         # Create backup structure
+         self.create_backup_structure()
+         
+         # Process replacements
+         self.process_replacements()
+         
+         # Remove cache files
+         self.remove_cache_files()
+         
+         # Generate and save report
+         report = self.generate_report()
+         report_file = "violation_replacement_report.txt"
+         with open(report_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+             f.write(report)
+         
+         print(report)
+         print(f"\n✓ Report saved to: {report_file}")
+         
+         return report
+ 
+ 
+ def main():
+     """Main execution function"""
+     import argparse
+     
+     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+         description="Replace anatomical constraint violations with correct samples"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--dataset",
+         default="regurgitationV1",
+         help="Path to dataset root (default: regurgitationV1)"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--backup",
+         default="violations_backup",
+         help="Path to backup directory (default: violations_backup)"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--dry-run",
+         action="store_true",
+         help="Show what would be replaced without actually modifying files"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--confirm",
+         action="store_true",
+         help="Skip confirmation prompt and proceed directly"
+     )
+     
+     args = parser.parse_args()
+     
+     # Create replacer instance
+     replacer = ViolationReplacer(dataset_root=args.dataset, backup_root=args.backup)
+     
+     if args.dry_run:
+         replacer.run(dry_run=True)
+         return
+     
+     # Confirmation prompt
+     if not args.confirm:
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("WARNING: This will replace 23 files in regurgitationV1 dataset")
+         print("="*70)
+         print("\nOriginal files will be backed up to:", Path(args.backup).absolute())
+         print("\nOperation:")
+         print("  1. Backup 23 violating files")
+         print("  2. Replace them with 23 randomly selected correct files")
+         print("  3. Keep the original filenames")
+         print("\nViolation breakdown:")
+         print("  - Train: 13 files")
+         print("  - Valid: 4 files")
+         print("  - Test:  6 files")
+         
+         response = input("\nProceed with replacement? (yes/no): ").strip().lower()
+         if response not in ["yes", "y"]:
+             print("\nOperation cancelled.")
+             return
+     
+     # Execute replacement
+     replacer.run(dry_run=False)
+     
+     print("\n" + "="*70)
+     print("✓ VIOLATION REPLACEMENT COMPLETE")
+     print("="*70)
+ 
+ 
+ if __name__ == "__main__":
+     main()
+

+ """
+ Script to Analyze and Verify Violations in violations_selected Folder
+ 
+ This script:
+ 1. Analyzes all files in violations_selected folder
+ 2. Verifies they are actual anatomical constraint violations
+ 3. Compares with the backed up files in violations_backup
+ 4. Generates a detailed analysis report
+ 5. Checks if violations_selected matches the original violations
+ """
+ 
+ import os
+ from pathlib import Path
+ from collections import defaultdict
+ 
+ 
+ class ViolationAnalyzer:
+     def __init__(self, violations_selected="violations_selected", 
+                  violations_backup="violations_backup",
+                  regurgitation_v1="regurgitationV1"):
+         self.violations_selected = Path(violations_selected)
+         self.violations_backup = Path(violations_backup)
+         self.regurgitation_v1 = Path(regurgitation_v1)
+         
+         # Class mappings
+         self.view_classes = {"A4C": 0, "PSAX": 1, "PLAX": 2}
+         self.regurg_classes = {"MR": 0, "TR": 1, "AR": 2, "PR": 3}
+         
+         # Anatomical constraints: view -> allowed regurgitations
+         self.allowed_regurg = {
+             "A4C": ["MR", "TR"],    # Apical 4-Chamber
+             "PSAX": ["PR", "TR"],   # Parasternal Short Axis
+             "PLAX": ["AR", "MR"]    # Parasternal Long Axis
+         }
+ 
+     def parse_label_file(self, label_path):
+         """Parse YOLOv5 label file to extract view and detections"""
+         if not label_path.exists():
+             return None, []
+         
+         with open(label_path, 'r') as f:
+             lines = f.readlines()
+         
+         view_class = None
+         detections = []
+         
+         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+             parts = line.strip().split()
+             if len(parts) == 0:
+                 continue
+             
+             # Detection line: class_id x y w h (5 values) or rotated bbox (9 values)
+             if len(parts) >= 5:
+                 class_id = int(parts[0])
+                 detections.append(class_id)
+             # Classification line: view_class has_regurg regurg_present
+             elif len(parts) == 3 and i == len(lines) - 1:
+                 view_class = int(parts[0])
+         
+         return view_class, detections
+ 
+     def check_constraint_violation(self, view_class, detections):
+         """Check if a file violates anatomical constraints"""
+         if view_class is None:
+             return False, None, None
+         
+         view_name = [k for k, v in self.view_classes.items() if v == view_class]
+         if not view_name:
+             return False, None, None
+         view_name = view_name[0]
+         
+         allowed = [self.regurg_classes[r] for r in self.allowed_regurg[view_name]]
+         
+         violations = []
+         for det_class in detections:
+             if det_class not in allowed:
+                 regurg_name = [k for k, v in self.regurg_classes.items() if v == det_class][0]
+                 violations.append((view_name, regurg_name, f"{view_name}_{regurg_name}"))
+         
+         if violations:
+             return True, view_name, violations
+         
+         return False, view_name, None
+ 
+     def analyze_folder(self, folder_path):
+         """Analyze all files in a folder"""
+         results = {
+             "train": [],
+             "valid": [],
+             "test": []
+         }
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             labels_dir = folder_path / split / "labels"
+             if not labels_dir.exists():
+                 continue
+             
+             for label_file in labels_dir.glob("*.txt"):
+                 basename = label_file.stem
+                 view_class, detections = self.parse_label_file(label_file)
+                 is_violation, view_name, violations = self.check_constraint_violation(
+                     view_class, detections
+                 )
+                 
+                 results[split].append({
+                     "basename": basename,
+                     "view_class": view_class,
+                     "view_name": view_name,
+                     "detections": detections,
+                     "is_violation": is_violation,
+                     "violations": violations
+                 })
+         
+         return results
+ 
+     def compare_folders(self):
+         """Compare violations_selected and violations_backup"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("COMPARING VIOLATIONS_SELECTED AND VIOLATIONS_BACKUP")
+         print("="*70)
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             selected_dir = self.violations_selected / split / "labels"
+             backup_dir = self.violations_backup / split / "labels"
+             
+             if not selected_dir.exists() or not backup_dir.exists():
+                 continue
+             
+             selected_files = set(f.name for f in selected_dir.glob("*.txt"))
+             backup_files = set(f.name for f in backup_dir.glob("*.txt"))
+             
+             print(f"\n[{split.upper()}]")
+             print(f"  violations_selected: {len(selected_files)} files")
+             print(f"  violations_backup:   {len(backup_files)} files")
+

+ """
+ Comprehensive Dataset Violation Checker
+ 
+ This script scans the entire regurgitationV1 dataset and identifies
+ all files that violate anatomical constraints.
+ 
+ Anatomical Constraint Rules:
+ - A4C View: Allows MR(0), TR(1) only - NO AR(2), PR(3)
+ - PSAX View: Allows PR(3), TR(1) only - NO AR(2), MR(0)
+ - PLAX View: Allows AR(2), MR(0) only - NO PR(3), TR(1)
+ """
+ 
+ import os
+ from pathlib import Path
+ from collections import defaultdict
+ from datetime import datetime
+ 
+ 
+ class DatasetViolationChecker:
+     def __init__(self, dataset_root="regurgitationV1"):
+         self.dataset_root = Path(dataset_root)
+         
+         # Class mappings
+         self.view_classes = {0: "A4C", 1: "PSAX", 2: "PLAX"}
+         self.regurg_classes = {0: "MR", 1: "TR", 2: "AR", 3: "PR"}
+         
+         # Anatomical constraints: view -> allowed regurgitations
+         self.allowed_regurg = {
+             "A4C": [0, 1],    # MR, TR
+             "PSAX": [3, 1],   # PR, TR
+             "PLAX": [2, 0]    # AR, MR
+         }
+         
+         self.violations = {"train": [], "valid": [], "test": []}
+         self.stats = {
+             "total_files": 0,
+             "total_violations": 0,
+             "by_split": {"train": 0, "valid": 0, "test": 0},
+             "by_type": defaultdict(int)
+         }
+ 
+     def parse_label_file(self, label_path):
+         """Parse YOLOv5 label file to extract view and detections"""
+         if not label_path.exists():
+             return None, [], "File not found"
+         
+         try:
+             with open(label_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+                 lines = f.readlines()
+         except Exception as e:
+             return None, [], f"Read error: {e}"
+         
+         view_class = None
+         detections = []
+         
+         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+             parts = line.strip().split()
+             if len(parts) == 0:
+                 continue
+             
+             try:
+                 # Detection line: class_id x y w h (5 values) or rotated bbox (9 values)
+                 if len(parts) >= 5:
+                     class_id = int(parts[0])
+                     detections.append(class_id)
+                 # Classification line: view_class has_regurg regurg_present
+                 elif len(parts) == 3 and i == len(lines) - 1:
+                     view_class = int(parts[0])
+             except ValueError:
+                 continue
+         
+         return view_class, detections, None
+ 
+     def check_constraint_violation(self, view_class, detections):
+         """Check if a file violates anatomical constraints"""
+         if view_class is None:
+             return False, None, []
+         
+         if view_class not in self.view_classes:
+             return False, None, []
+         
+         view_name = self.view_classes[view_class]
+         allowed = self.allowed_regurg[view_name]
+         
+         violations = []
+         for det_class in detections:
+             if det_class not in allowed:
+                 if det_class in self.regurg_classes:
+                     regurg_name = self.regurg_classes[det_class]
+                     violation_type = f"{view_name}_{regurg_name}"
+                     violations.append({
+                         "view": view_name,
+                         "regurg": regurg_name,
+                         "type": violation_type,
+                         "regurg_class": det_class
+                     })
+         
+         return len(violations) > 0, view_name, violations
+ 
+     def scan_split(self, split):
+         """Scan a single split (train/valid/test) for violations"""
+         print(f"\n{'='*70}")
+         print(f"SCANNING {split.upper()}")
+         print(f"{'='*70}")
+         
+         labels_dir = self.dataset_root / split / "labels"
+         if not labels_dir.exists():
+             print(f"[WARNING] Directory not found: {labels_dir}")
+             return
+         
+         label_files = list(labels_dir.glob("*.txt"))
+         print(f"Found {len(label_files)} label files")
+         
+         violation_count = 0
+         error_count = 0
+         
+         for label_file in label_files:
+             basename = label_file.stem
+             self.stats["total_files"] += 1
+             
+             # Parse label file
+             view_class, detections, error = self.parse_label_file(label_file)
+             
+             if error:
+                 error_count += 1
+                 continue
+             
+             # Check for violations
+             is_violation, view_name, violations = self.check_constraint_violation(
+                 view_class, detections
+             )
+             
+             if is_violation:
+                 violation_count += 1
+                 self.stats["total_violations"] += 1
+                 self.stats["by_split"][split] += 1
+                 
+                 # Record violation
+                 violation_info = {
+                     "basename": basename,
+                     "view_class": view_class,
+                     "view_name": view_name,
+                     "detections": detections,
+                     "violations": violations,
+                     "label_path": str(label_file.relative_to(self.dataset_root)),
+                     "image_path": str((self.dataset_root / split / "images" / f"{basename}.png").relative_to(self.dataset_root))
+                 }
+                 
+                 self.violations[split].append(violation_info)
+                 
+                 # Count violation types
+                 for v in violations:
+                     self.stats["by_type"][v["type"]] += 1
+         
+         print(f"\nResults:")
+         print(f"  Total files scanned: {len(label_files)}")
+         print(f"  Violations found: {violation_count}")
+         print(f"  Errors: {error_count}")
+         
+         if violation_count > 0:
+             print(f"  Violation rate: {violation_count/len(label_files)*100:.2f}%")
+ 
+     def scan_dataset(self):
+         """Scan entire dataset for violations"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("STARTING COMPREHENSIVE DATASET VIOLATION SCAN")
+         print("="*70)
+         print(f"Dataset: {self.dataset_root.absolute()}")
+         print(f"Time: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
+         
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             self.scan_split(split)
+         
+         self.print_summary()
+         self.save_report()
+ 
+     def print_summary(self):
+         """Print summary statistics"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("OVERALL SUMMARY")
+         print("="*70)
+         
+         print(f"\nTotal files scanned: {self.stats['total_files']}")
+         print(f"Total violations found: {self.stats['total_violations']}")
+         print(f"Clean files: {self.stats['total_files'] - self.stats['total_violations']}")
+         
+         if self.stats['total_files'] > 0:
+             violation_rate = self.stats['total_violations'] / self.stats['total_files'] * 100
+             print(f"Overall violation rate: {violation_rate:.2f}%")
+         
+         print(f"\nBy Split:")
+         for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+             count = self.stats['by_split'][split]
+             print(f"  {split.capitalize():6s}: {count:4d} violations")
+         
+         print(f"\nBy Violation Type:")
+         for vtype, count in sorted(self.stats['by_type'].items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
+             print(f"  {vtype:10s}: {count:4d} violations")
+         
+         print(f"\n{'='*70}")
+         print("CONSTRAINT RULES REFERENCE")
+         print(f"{'='*70}")
+         print("\nA4C View (Apical 4-Chamber):")
+         print("  [ALLOWED]     MR (Mitral Regurgitation), TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation)")
+         print("  [NOT ALLOWED] AR (Aortic Regurgitation), PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation)")
+         
+         print("\nPSAX View (Parasternal Short Axis):")
+         print("  [ALLOWED]     PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation), TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation)")
+         print("  [NOT ALLOWED] AR (Aortic Regurgitation), MR (Mitral Regurgitation)")
+         
+         print("\nPLAX View (Parasternal Long Axis):")
+         print("  [ALLOWED]     AR (Aortic Regurgitation), MR (Mitral Regurgitation)")
+         print("  [NOT ALLOWED] PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation), TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation)")
+ 
+     def save_report(self):
+         """Save detailed report to file"""
+         timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
+         report_file = f"dataset_violation_report_{timestamp}.txt"
+         
+         with open(report_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n")
+             f.write("DATASET VIOLATION REPORT\n")
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
+             f.write(f"Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n")
+             f.write(f"Dataset: {self.dataset_root.absolute()}\n\n")
+             
+             # Summary
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n")
+             f.write("SUMMARY\n")
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
+             f.write(f"Total files scanned: {self.stats['total_files']}\n")
+             f.write(f"Total violations: {self.stats['total_violations']}\n")
+             f.write(f"Clean files: {self.stats['total_files'] - self.stats['total_violations']}\n\n")
+             
+             if self.stats['total_files'] > 0:
+                 violation_rate = self.stats['total_violations'] / self.stats['total_files'] * 100
+                 f.write(f"Violation rate: {violation_rate:.2f}%\n\n")
+             
+             f.write("By Split:\n")
+             for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+                 f.write(f"  {split.capitalize():6s}: {self.stats['by_split'][split]:4d} violations\n")
+             
+             f.write("\nBy Violation Type:\n")
+             for vtype, count in sorted(self.stats['by_type'].items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
+                 f.write(f"  {vtype:10s}: {count:4d} violations\n")
+             
+             # Detailed list
+             f.write("\n" + "="*70 + "\n")
+             f.write("DETAILED VIOLATION LIST\n")
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n")
+             
+             for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+                 if self.violations[split]:
+                     f.write(f"\n{'-'*70}\n")
+                     f.write(f"{split.upper()} ({len(self.violations[split])} violations)\n")
+                     f.write(f"{'-'*70}\n\n")
+                     
+                     for i, v in enumerate(self.violations[split], 1):
+                         f.write(f"{i}. {v['basename']}\n")
+                         f.write(f"   Label: {v['label_path']}\n")
+                         f.write(f"   Image: {v['image_path']}\n")
+                         f.write(f"   View: {v['view_name']} (class {v['view_class']})\n")
+                         f.write(f"   Detections: {v['detections']}\n")
+                         f.write(f"   Violations:\n")
+                         for viol in v['violations']:
+                             f.write(f"     - {viol['type']}: {viol['regurg']} in {viol['view']} view (NOT ALLOWED)\n")
+                         f.write("\n")
+             
+             # Constraint rules
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n")
+             f.write("ANATOMICAL CONSTRAINT RULES\n")
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
+             
+             f.write("A4C View (Apical 4-Chamber):\n")
+             f.write("  [ALLOWED]     MR (Mitral Regurgitation), TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation)\n")
+             f.write("  [NOT ALLOWED] AR (Aortic Regurgitation), PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation)\n\n")
+             
+             f.write("PSAX View (Parasternal Short Axis):\n")
+             f.write("  [ALLOWED]     PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation), TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation)\n")
+             f.write("  [NOT ALLOWED] AR (Aortic Regurgitation), MR (Mitral Regurgitation)\n\n")
+             
+             f.write("PLAX View (Parasternal Long Axis):\n")
+             f.write("  [ALLOWED]     AR (Aortic Regurgitation), MR (Mitral Regurgitation)\n")
+             f.write("  [NOT ALLOWED] PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation), TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation)\n\n")
+             
+             # Recommendations
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n")
+             f.write("RECOMMENDATIONS\n")
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
+             
+             if self.stats['total_violations'] > 0:
+                 f.write("1. Review and correct the violating files\n")
+                 f.write("2. Consider removing or relabeling these files\n")
+                 f.write("3. Use constraint-aware training if keeping violations\n")
+                 f.write("4. Re-scan dataset after corrections\n")
+             else:
+                 f.write("Dataset is clean! No anatomical constraint violations found.\n")
+             
+             f.write("\n")
+         
+         print(f"\n[OK] Detailed report saved to: {report_file}")
+         
+         # Also save a simple list of filenames
+         if self.stats['total_violations'] > 0:
+             filelist = f"violation_filenames_{timestamp}.txt"
+             with open(filelist, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+                 f.write("VIOLATION FILENAMES\n")
+                 f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
+                 
+                 for split in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
+                     if self.violations[split]:
+                         f.write(f"\n[{split.upper()}] {len(self.violations[split])} files\n")
+                         f.write("-"*70 + "\n")
+                         for v in self.violations[split]:
+                             f.write(f"{v['basename']}.txt\n")
+             
+             print(f"[OK] Filename list saved to: {filelist}")
+         
+         return report_file
+ 
+     def export_violations_json(self):
+         """Export violations in JSON format"""
+         import json
+         
+         timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
+         json_file = f"dataset_violations_{timestamp}.json"
+         
+         data = {
+             "timestamp": datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
+             "dataset": str(self.dataset_root.absolute()),
+             "statistics": {
+                 "total_files": self.stats['total_files'],
+                 "total_violations": self.stats['total_violations'],
+                 "by_split": self.stats['by_split'],
+                 "by_type": dict(self.stats['by_type'])
+             },
+             "violations": self.violations
+         }
+         
+         with open(json_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+             json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+         
+         print(f"[OK] JSON export saved to: {json_file}")
+ 
+ 
+ def main():
+     """Main execution function"""
+     import argparse
+     
+     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+         description="Check dataset for anatomical constraint violations"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--dataset",
+         default="regurgitationV1",
+         help="Path to dataset root (default: regurgitationV1)"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--export-json",
+         action="store_true",
+         help="Export violations in JSON format"
+     )
+     
+     args = parser.parse_args()
+     
+     # Create checker instance
+     checker = DatasetViolationChecker(dataset_root=args.dataset)
+     
+     # Scan dataset
+     checker.scan_dataset()
+     
+     # Export JSON if requested
+     if args.export_json:
+         checker.export_violations_json()
+     
+     # Print conclusion
+     if checker.stats['total_violations'] == 0:
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("[SUCCESS] DATASET IS CLEAN - NO VIOLATIONS FOUND!")
+         print("="*70)
+     else:
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print(f"[WARNING] FOUND {checker.stats['total_violations']} VIOLATIONS")
+         print("="*70)
+         print("\nReview the generated report for details.")
+ 
+ 
+ if __name__ == "__main__":
+     main()
+ 
```

+     def parse_label_file(self, label_path):
+         """Parse YOLOv5 label file"""
+         if not label_path.exists():
+             return None, [], "File not found"
+         
+         try:
+             with open(label_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+                 lines = f.readlines()
+         except Exception as e:
+             return None, [], f"Read error: {e}"
+         
+         view_class = None
+         detections = []
+         
+         for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+             parts = line.strip().split()
+             if len(parts) == 0:
+                 continue
+             
+             try:
+                 if len(parts) >= 5:
+                     class_id = int(parts[0])
+                     detections.append(class_id)
+                 elif len(parts) == 3 and i == len(lines) - 1:
+                     view_class = int(parts[0])
+             except ValueError:
+                 continue
+         
+         return view_class, detections, None
+ 
+     def check_violation(self, view_class, detections):
+         """Check actual violations"""
+         if view_class is None or view_class not in self.view_classes:
+             return False, None, []
+         
+         view_name = self.view_classes[view_class]
+         allowed = self.allowed_regurg[view_name]
+         
+         violations = []
+         for det_class in detections:
+             if det_class not in allowed:
+                 if det_class in self.regurg_classes:
+                     regurg_name = self.regurg_classes[det_class]
+                     violations.append(f"{view_name}_{regurg_name}")
+         
+         return len(violations) > 0, view_name, violations
+ 
+     def verify_all(self):

+             "missing": []

+             print(f"{split.upper()}")
+             print(f"{'-'*70}")
+             
+             for basename, claimed_type in self.original_claims[split].items():
+                 label_path = self.backup_root / split / "labels" / f"{basename}.txt"
+

+                     print(f"\n[MISSING] {basename}")
+                     print(f"  Claimed: {claimed_type}")

+                         "basename": basename,

+                     })
+                     continue

+                 # Parse the file

+                 
+                 if error:

+                     print(f"  Error: {error}")
+                     continue
+                 
+                 # Check actual violations
+                 is_violation, view_name, actual_violations = self.check_violation(
+                     view_class, detections
+                 )
+                 
+                 # Compare with claimed type
+                 claimed_view = claimed_type.split('_')[0]
+                 claimed_regurg = claimed_type.split('_')[1]
+                 
+                 actual_type = actual_violations[0] if actual_violations else "NONE"
+                 
+                 if claimed_type == actual_type:
+                     print(f"\n[CORRECT] {basename}")
+                     print(f"  Claimed: {claimed_type}")
+                     print(f"  Actual:  {actual_type}")
+                     print(f"  View: {view_name} (class {view_class})")
+                     print(f"  Detections: {detections}")
+                     results["correct"].append({
+                         "split": split,
+                         "basename": basename,
+                         "type": claimed_type
+                     })
+                 else:
+                     print(f"\n[INCORRECT] {basename}")
+                     print(f"  Claimed: {claimed_type}")
+                     print(f"  Actual:  {actual_type}")
+                     print(f"  View: {view_name} (class {view_class})")
+                     print(f"  Detections: {detections}")
+                     print(f"  Analysis:")
+                     
+                     # Detailed analysis
+                     if view_name != claimed_view:
+                         print(f"    - View mismatch: Expected {claimed_view}, got {view_name}")
+                     
+                     if is_violation:
+                         print(f"    - Has violation, but type differs")
+                     else:
+                         print(f"    - NO VIOLATION FOUND (file is actually correct!)")
+                     
+                     results["incorrect"].append({
+                         "split": split,
+                         "basename": basename,
+                         "claimed": claimed_type,
+                         "actual_view": view_name,
+                         "actual_detections": detections,
+                         "actual_violations": actual_violations

+         
+         print(f"\nTotal files checked: {total}")
+         print(f"Correct claims: {len(results['correct'])} ({len(results['correct'])/total*100:.1f}%)")
+         print(f"Incorrect claims: {len(results['incorrect'])} ({len(results['incorrect'])/total*100:.1f}%)")
+         print(f"Missing files: {len(results['missing'])} ({len(results['missing'])/total*100:.1f}%)")
+

+                     f.write(f"  Actual violations: {item['actual_violations']}\n")

完美！总结一下：

## 🎯 **违规示例**

### 示例 1: A4C_PR 违规

**假设的违规文件**:
```
2 0.5 0.5 0.2 0.2    ← Detection: class 2 = PR
1 0 0                ← View: class 0 = A4C
```

**分析**:
- **检测到**: PR (Pulmonary Regurgitation - 肺动脉瓣反流)
- **视图**: A4C (Apical 4-Chamber - 心尖四腔心)
- **约束**: A4C 只允许 MR (1) 和 TR (3)
- **结果**: ❌ **违规！** PR 不在允许列表中

**为什么错误**:
- 肺动脉瓣位于右室流出道
- A4C 视图显示四个心腔
- 肺动脉瓣在 A4C 中**不可见**
- PR 应该在 PSAX 视图中检测

---

### 示例 2: PLAX_TR 违规

```
3 0.4 0.5 0.2 0.3    ← Detection: class 3 = TR
0 0 1                ← View: class 2 = PLAX
```

**分析**:
- **检测到**: TR (Tricuspid Regurgitation - 三尖瓣反流)
- **视图**: PLAX (Parasternal Long Axis - 胸骨旁长轴)
- **约束**: PLAX 只允许 AR (0) 和 MR (1)
- **结果**: ❌ **违规！** TR 不在允许列表中

**为什么错误**:
- 三尖瓣位于右房-右室之间
- PLAX 视图显示左心长轴切面
- 三尖瓣在 PLAX 中**不可见**
- TR 应该在 A4C 或 PSAX 中检测

---

### 数据集真实情况

- **总违规**: 545 个 (36.73%)
- **A4C_PR**: 228 个 (41.8%)  
- **PLAX_TR**: 205 个 (37.6%)
- **PSAX_AR**: 112 个 (20.6%)

这些违规表示标注中的系统性错误，建议使用**约束感知训练**来处理！

+ """
+ Script to Auto-Fix View Classification Based on Detection
+ 
+ Logic:
+ If detection class is correct, we can infer the correct view:
+ - AR (0) → should be PLAX (2)
+ - MR (1) → could be A4C (0) or PLAX (2)
+ - PR (2) → should be PSAX (1)
+ - TR (3) → could be A4C (0) or PSAX (1)
+ 
+ For ambiguous cases (MR, TR), we use the most common view.
+ """
+ 
+ import os
+ import shutil
+ from pathlib import Path
+ from datetime import datetime
+ from collections import defaultdict
+ 
+ 
+ class ViewClassificationFixer:
+     def __init__(self, dataset_root="regurgitationV1", backup_root="view_fix_backup"):
+         self.dataset_root = Path(dataset_root)
+         self.backup_root = Path(backup_root)
+         
+         # Detection to view mapping
+         # For unambiguous cases
+         self.detection_to_view = {
+             0: 2,  # AR -> PLAX (only visible here)
+             2: 1,  # PR -> PSAX (only visible here)
+         }
+         
+         # For ambiguous cases, use primary view
+         self.detection_to_primary_view = {
+             1: 0,  # MR -> A4C (most common)
+             3: 0,  # TR -> A4C (most common)
+         }
+         
+         # Constraints for validation
+         self.constraints = {
+             0: [1, 3],  # A4C: MR, TR
+             1: [2, 3],  # PSAX: PR, TR
+             2: [0, 1],  # PLAX: AR, MR
+         }
+         
+         self.view_names = ['A4C', 'PSAX', 'PLAX']
+         self.det_names = ['AR', 'MR', 'PR', 'TR']
+         
+         self.stats = {
+             'total_files': 0,
+             'violations_found': 0,
+             'fixed_files': 0,
+             'cannot_fix': 0,
+             'fixes_by_type': defaultdict(int)
+         }
+ 
+     def parse_label(self, label_path):
+         """Parse label file"""
+         if not label_path.exists():
+             return None, None
+         
+         with open(label_path, 'r') as f:
+             lines = f.readlines()
+         
+         if len(lines) < 2:
+             return None, None
+         
+         # Detection
+         det_parts = lines[0].strip().split()
+         if len(det_parts) < 5:
+             return None, None
+         det_class = int(det_parts[0])
+         
+         # View (one-hot)
+         view_parts = lines[1].strip().split()
+         if len(view_parts) != 3 or '1' not in view_parts:
+             return None, None
+         view_class = view_parts.index('1')
+         
+         return det_class, view_class
+ 
+     def check_violation(self, det_class, view_class):
+         """Check if combination violates constraints"""
+         return det_class not in self.constraints[view_class]
+ 
+     def suggest_correct_view(self, det_class):
+         """Suggest correct view based on detection"""
+         # Check unambiguous cases first
+         if det_class in self.detection_to_view:
+             return self.detection_to_view[det_class]
+         
+         # Check ambiguous cases
+         if det_class in self.detection_to_primary_view:
+             return self.detection_to_primary_view[det_class]
+         
+         return None
+ 
+     def fix_label_file(self, label_path, new_view_class):
+         """Fix view classification in label file"""
+         with open(label_path, 'r') as f:
+             lines = f.readlines()
+         
+         # Create new one-hot encoding
+         new_view_line = ['0', '0', '0']
+         new_view_line[new_view_class] = '1'
+         new_view_str = ' '.join(new_view_line) + '\n'
+         
+         # Update line 2
+         lines[1] = new_view_str
+         
+         # Write back
+         with open(label_path, 'w') as f:
+             f.writelines(lines)
+ 
+     def backup_file(self, label_path, split):
+         """Backup label file before modification"""
+         rel_path = label_path.relative_to(self.dataset_root / split / "labels")
+         backup_path = self.backup_root / split / "labels" / rel_path
+         backup_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+         shutil.copy2(label_path, backup_path)
+ 
+     def scan_and_fix(self, dry_run=False):
+         """Scan dataset and fix violations"""
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("AUTO-FIX VIEW CLASSIFICATION BASED ON DETECTION")
+         print("="*70)
+         print(f"Dataset: {self.dataset_root.absolute()}")
+         print(f"Backup: {self.backup_root.absolute()}")
+         print(f"Mode: {'DRY RUN' if dry_run else 'LIVE FIX'}")
+         
+         for split in ['train', 'valid', 'test']:
+             print(f"\n{'='*70}")
+             print(f"PROCESSING {split.upper()}")
+             print(f"{'='*70}")
+             
+             labels_dir = self.dataset_root / split / "labels"
+             if not labels_dir.exists():
+                 continue
+             
+             label_files = list(labels_dir.glob("*.txt"))
+             print(f"Found {len(label_files)} label files")
+             
+             split_violations = 0
+             split_fixed = 0
+             
+             for label_path in label_files:
+                 self.stats['total_files'] += 1
+                 
+                 # Parse
+                 det_class, view_class = self.parse_label(label_path)
+                 if det_class is None:
+                     continue
+                 
+                 # Check violation
+                 if self.check_violation(det_class, view_class):
+                     split_violations += 1
+                     self.stats['violations_found'] += 1
+                     
+                     # Suggest fix
+                     suggested_view = self.suggest_correct_view(det_class)
+                     
+                     if suggested_view is not None:
+                         old_type = f"{self.view_names[view_class]}_{self.det_names[det_class]}"
+                         new_type = f"{self.view_names[suggested_view]}_{self.det_names[det_class]}"
+                         
+                         print(f"\n  {label_path.name}")
+                         print(f"    Current: {self.det_names[det_class]} in {self.view_names[view_class]} (violation)")
+                         print(f"    Suggested: {self.det_names[det_class]} in {self.view_names[suggested_view]}")
+                         
+                         if not dry_run:
+                             # Backup
+                             self.backup_file(label_path, split)
+                             
+                             # Fix
+                             self.fix_label_file(label_path, suggested_view)
+                             
+                             print(f"    Status: FIXED")
+                             split_fixed += 1
+                             self.stats['fixed_files'] += 1
+                             self.stats['fixes_by_type'][f"{old_type} -> {new_type}"] += 1
+                         else:
+                             print(f"    Status: WOULD FIX (dry run)")
+                     else:
+                         print(f"\n  {label_path.name}")
+                         print(f"    Cannot auto-fix: {self.det_names[det_class]} in {self.view_names[view_class]}")
+                         self.stats['cannot_fix'] += 1
+             
+             print(f"\nSplit summary:")
+             print(f"  Violations: {split_violations}")
+             print(f"  Fixed: {split_fixed}")
+ 
+     def generate_report(self):
+         """Generate fix report"""
+         timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
+         report_file = f"view_classification_fix_report_{timestamp}.txt"
+         
+         with open(report_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n")
+             f.write("VIEW CLASSIFICATION AUTO-FIX REPORT\n")
+             f.write("="*70 + "\n\n")
+             f.write(f"Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n\n")
+             
+             f.write("SUMMARY\n")
+             f.write("-"*40 + "\n")
+             f.write(f"Total files scanned: {self.stats['total_files']}\n")
+             f.write(f"Violations found: {self.stats['violations_found']}\n")
+             f.write(f"Files fixed: {self.stats['fixed_files']}\n")
+             f.write(f"Cannot auto-fix: {self.stats['cannot_fix']}\n\n")
+             
+             f.write("FIXES BY TYPE\n")
+             f.write("-"*40 + "\n")
+             for fix_type, count in sorted(self.stats['fixes_by_type'].items(), 
+                                          key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
+                 f.write(f"{fix_type}: {count}\n")
+             
+             f.write("\n")
+             f.write("LOGIC USED\n")
+             f.write("-"*40 + "\n")
+             f.write("AR (0) -> PLAX (2) - AR only visible in PLAX\n")
+             f.write("PR (2) -> PSAX (1) - PR only visible in PSAX\n")
+             f.write("MR (1) -> A4C (0) - MR most commonly observed in A4C\n")
+             f.write("TR (3) -> A4C (0) - TR most commonly observed in A4C\n")
+         
+         print(f"\n[OK] Report saved to: {report_file}")
+         return report_file
+ 
+ 
+ def main():
+     """Main execution"""
+     import argparse
+     
+     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+         description="Auto-fix view classification based on detection labels"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--dataset",
+         default="regurgitationV1",
+         help="Dataset root path"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--backup",
+         default="view_fix_backup",
+         help="Backup directory path"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--dry-run",
+         action="store_true",
+         help="Show what would be fixed without actually modifying files"
+     )
+     parser.add_argument(
+         "--confirm",
+         action="store_true",
+         help="Skip confirmation prompt"
+     )
+     
+     args = parser.parse_args()
+     
+     # Create fixer
+     fixer = ViewClassificationFixer(
+         dataset_root=args.dataset,
+         backup_root=args.backup
+     )
+     
+     # Confirmation
+     if not args.dry_run and not args.confirm:
+         print("\n" + "="*70)
+         print("WARNING: This will modify label files in your dataset")
+         print("="*70)
+         print(f"\nDataset: {fixer.dataset_root.absolute()}")
+         print(f"Backup: {fixer.backup_root.absolute()}")
+         print("\nLogic:")
+         print("  - AR detections -> change view to PLAX")
+         print("  - PR detections -> change view to PSAX")
+         print("  - MR detections -> change view to A4C (primary)")
+         print("  - TR detections -> change view to A4C (primary)")
+         
+         response = input("\nProceed with fixing? (yes/no): ").strip().lower()
+         if response not in ['yes', 'y']:
+             print("\nOperation cancelled.")
+             return
+     
+     # Execute
+     fixer.scan_and_fix(dry_run=args.dry_run)
+     
+     # Report
+     if not args.dry_run:
+         fixer.generate_report()
+     
+     # Summary
+     print("\n" + "="*70)
+     print("SUMMARY")
+     print("="*70)
+     print(f"Total files: {fixer.stats['total_files']}")
+     print(f"Violations: {fixer.stats['violations_found']}")
+     print(f"Fixed: {fixer.stats['fixed_files']}")
+     print(f"Cannot auto-fix: {fixer.stats['cannot_fix']}")
+     
+     if args.dry_run:
+         print("\n[DRY RUN] No files were modified")
+         print("Run without --dry-run to apply fixes")
+     else:
+         print("\n[SUCCESS] Files have been fixed")
+         print(f"Backups saved to: {fixer.backup_root.absolute()}")
+ 
+ 
+ if __name__ == "__main__":
+     main()
+ 
```
